title: Chicken drumstick, fried, coated, skinless, coating eaten, from raw

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken drumsticks that are deep‑fried in a crispy coating are juicy inside and flavorful outside. The coating, usually made from flour, spices and sometimes breadcrumbs, is completely edible. This product is commonly served as a snack or main dish in fast‑food restaurants and home kitchens.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks contain more connective tissue than breast meat, which makes them especially moist after frying.
Deep‑frying at 175‑190 °C creates a golden crust while sealing in moisture.
Coatings often include paprika, garlic, onion, and black pepper for extra flavor.
In many cuisines the drumsticks are served with barbecue, honey‑mustard, or spicy chili sauces.
Chicken drumsticks are a key ingredient in dishes like paprikash, chicken stew, and many Asian stir‑fries.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken drumsticks provide high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain niacin (B3), vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Phosphorus, selenium and zinc in the meat contribute to bone health, immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Ideal for low‑carb diets as they provide energy without significant carbs.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: Protein and a modest amount of fat help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds saturated and possibly trans fats, so consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: The coating often contains salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor salmonella; ensure internal temperature reaches 74 °C.

items.title: Allergy to coating ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to wheat, gluten or spices used in the breading.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried coated drumsticks can be enjoyed hot as a standalone dish, served with potatoes, rice or vegetable sides. They are often paired with sauces such as barbecue, honey‑mustard, garlic aioli or spicy chili sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked drumsticks in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a bag at –18 °C, where they retain quality for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.
